speaker: Doctor
text: Good morning. I see you are experiencing right groin pain and had to hold your leg in an abnormal position after the collision. To better understand your injury, how did this position feel at the moment of impact, and were you able to move the leg normally afterward?

speaker: Patient
text: 25-year-old female. The patient was involved in a rear-end collision where she was the restrained driver of the back car. She reports immediate onset of pain in both knees and severe pain over the right groin area following the accident.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Did you hear a loud "pop" or "snap" sound at the moment of impact when your leg went into that abnormal position? Additionally, can you currently bear any weight on your right leg, and does moving it outward cause sharp pain?

REQUEST TEST: X-Ray of the right pelvis and hip.
REQUEST IMAGES: Pelvic_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Pelvic_X-ray Findings: No fractures identified in the pelvic ring or femoral neck, but alignment suggests posterior dislocation of the right hip.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Severe right groin pain. I also have Pain in both knees, Right leg is slightly shortened, flexed, adducted, and internally rotated.

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: No significant past medical history. Social history: Works as an elementary school teacher. Non-smoker and drinks alcohol socially.

speaker: Patient
text: Alert and active. No head injury, abdominal pain, or chest pain reported. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Posterior Wall Acetabular Fracture with Posterior Hip Dislocation.

The mechanism of a rear-end collision causing immediate severe groin pain followed by an inability to move the leg typically suggests a posterior hip dislocation, often accompanied by an acetabular fracture. The "abnormal position" you described was likely the leg being forced into flexion, abduction, and external rotation, which is classic for this injury. I have requested the images; if they confirm the hip is out of place and the bone is cracked, we will need immediate surgical reduction to prevent permanent nerve damage and joint destruction.
